arguments.heading: What happened at the argument

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: California law requires licensed pro-life centers to direct patients to abortion services. It also imposes strict advertising rules on unlicensed centers. The state exempts other medical providers from these rules. the sides that brought the case claim this targets their speech. The state argues it serves public health interests.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the limits of state power to compel speech. It affects how states regulate medical and non-medical providers. It determines whether targeted disclosures violate constitutional rights. The outcome shapes future regulations on patient information.
